clue.text: Its perpetrator won't give the Inland Revenue its due

definitions.text: Its perpetrator won't give the Inland Revenue its due

parts.words: Its perpetrator won't give the Inland Revenue its due
parts.note: describes a scheme for dodging what is owed to the British tax authority, read from the side of the one who runs it

explanation.surface: A description of someone cheating the British taxman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was the UK's tax-collecting department; the scheme that cheats it is the answer, though 'perpetrator' makes you look for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest arrangement for underpaying tax is what deprives the Revenue of its due.

clue.text: Correct definition of noon

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry for midday is being put right.
explanation.walkthrough: Noon is the moment the morning, a.m., finishes, so it can be described as the a.m. end; run together that gives a verb meaning correct.
explanation.definitionFit: To put right or revise is to correct; and midday closes the morning hours, abbreviated a.m.

clue.text: Iron Cross for capping a pair of scissors

indicators.note: in a down answer the word for sits on top, capping the pieces that follow it

parts.note: taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a cross is drawn as the letter X

explanation.surface: A medal, the Iron Cross, awarded for topping off a pair of scissors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Cross' reads as the German medal but splits into FE and X.
explanation.definitionFit: Forfex is the Latin-derived term for shears or pincers, as on an earwig's tail.

clue.text: US handbill advertising an artful Dickens character

explanation.surface: An American flyer promoting a crafty figure from Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advertising' links the two senses; the Artful Dodger is the young pickpocket in Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a small printed advertising leaflet is called this; and the Artful one is Fagin's pickpocket lad in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Advance payments

parts.note: money handed over ahead, to be paid back later, as a bank does to borrowers

explanation.definitionFit: Sums lent are advances of money to be repaid, so they are payments made in advance.

clue.text: He sunset trail that takes one out of London

definitions.text: He sunset trail that takes one out of London

parts.words: He sunset trail that takes one out of London
parts.note: a route heading towards the setting sun from the capital, an arterial highway

explanation.surface: A romantic picture of riding off into the sunset from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The sun sets in the west, so the 'sunset trail' is the major road running west out of London (the A4).
explanation.definitionFit: The A4 arterial highway leading westward from the capital bears this name.

clue.text: Type of listed building in which Stalin was born?

definitions.text: Type of listed building in which Stalin was born?

parts.words: Type of listed building in which Stalin was born?
parts.note: an 18th-century architectural style shares its name with the Caucasian country of Stalin's birth

explanation.surface: A heritage question about Stalin's birthplace.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'listed building' is one protected in Britain for its historic value; the period style named after the Hanoverian kings also names Stalin's homeland, Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Homes of the 1714-1830 era are a common protected category, and a dwelling in Stalin's homeland could be called this too.

clue.text: Region that has no traffic restrictions

definitions.text: Region that has no traffic restrictions

parts.words: Region that has no traffic restrictions
parts.note: traffic here is commerce between nations, not cars, so a zone without tariffs or quotas

explanation.surface: A road zone with no driving rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' suggests vehicles but means trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of countries that remove tariffs and quotas on commerce among themselves forms such a zone.

clue.text: Close of play in theatreland

parts.note: the final performance ending a stage production's run

explanation.surface: Stumps being drawn, as in cricket, but in the West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close of play' is the cricket term for the end of a day's game, but here a play closes at its final performance.
explanation.definitionFit: The closing performance of a show's run is its final evening on stage.

clue.text: Spruced up group of tradesmen

indicators.note: to group things is to arrange them anew, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A band of tradesmen who have been tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group' looks like a noun belonging with 'tradesmen'; it tells you to rearrange TRADESMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarten is to tidy or make neater, so spruced up and smartened are synonyms.

clue.text: Kind of prize that's apparently a drawback

definitions.text: Kind of prize that's apparently a drawback

parts.words: Kind of prize that's apparently a drawback
parts.note: read 'drawback' as 'draw' written backwards after 'a', and a prize appears

explanation.surface: A prize that turns out to be a disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawback is a snag, but split it: DRAW back is WARD, and A before it gives a word for a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize or decoration granted by judges is a synonym for the answer.

clue.text: Sheepish male confronted with Civil Service return? Get away with you!

indicators.note: the Civil Service letters make a return, read from right to left

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An awkward man faced with a government form is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' suggests shyness but means of sheep; 'Get away with you!' is an exclamation, so the answer is a command to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are brusque commands telling someone to go away at once.

clue.text: One must make some effort to do this oneself

definitions.text: One must make some effort to do this oneself

parts.words: One must make some effort to do this oneself
parts.note: points at a verb used with a reflexive pronoun meaning to try hard

explanation.surface: A truism about self-improvement taking effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb is used reflexively: to apply yourself strenuously.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain or apply oneself is to make an effort.

clue.text: A bird that makes us get excited about its content.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'A bird that makes us get excited about its content.', gives no parse for the bird that accounts for 'us' and 'about its content'; an anagram of 'greet' fits but the clue prints 'get'.
annotationWithheld.clue: A bird that makes us get excited about its content.

clue.text: … and one from whose plumage I derive comfort

indicators.note: the bird's name comes from a run of letters across the words plumage I derive

explanation.surface: A second bird, continuing the previous clue, whose feathers make comfortable bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' carries on from the bird in 13 Down; 'from' points to letters inside 'plumagE I DERive'. Eiderdown quilts give the 'comfort'.
explanation.definitionFit: Following the previous clue, one means another bird: the sea duck whose down fills quilts.

clue.text: Makes brisk progress among Labour's fringe supporters?

explanation.surface: The left wing of the Labour Party moving quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Trotskyists on the far-left fringe of Britain's Labour Party are nicknamed this; a horse also does it between a walk and a canter.
explanation.definitionFit: Moves at a jogging pace is the verb sense; Trotskyists on the far left are the slang noun.

clue.text: Employed as a haulage contractor?

parts.note: describes the activity of pulling a vehicle along behind a truck

explanation.surface: A question about a job at a road freight firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed' means in use: what a haulier's truck is doing when it pulls a load.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a load or vehicle by rope or chain is what a haulier does.

clue.text: An arm that's particularly slender

parts.note: arm in the sense of weapon, a narrow thrusting sword

explanation.surface: A remark about someone's thin limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' looks like the limb but is a weapon: a sword with a thin blade.
explanation.definitionFit: This light thrusting sword has a notably narrow blade, so it is a slim weapon.

clue.text: It may be slung from the shoulder these days in Rio

definitions.text: It may be slung from the shoulder

indicators.note: the letters for these days go inside the name Rio

parts.note: Rio, the Brazilian city, taken as written
AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Fashion in Rio de Janeiro, where things are carried over the shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these days' seems to belong to the shoulder-slung fashion but is the wordplay; 'in' puts it inside RIO. A portable set may hang from a shoulder strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable wireless set can be carried on a shoulder strap.

clue.text: Prudently take cover

parts.note: cover in the sense of a policy against loss, taken out as a sensible precaution

explanation.surface: A soldier wisely ducking for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take cover' suggests hiding, but cover is insurance protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying a policy against loss is taking out cover, a cautious step.

clue.text: An oppidan converted to wine

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so the letters of to wine are rearranged

explanation.surface: A city dweller who has taken up wine.
explanation.walkthrough: An oppidan is an inhabitant of a town (also a non-scholarship pupil at Eton).
explanation.definitionFit: Oppidan comes from Latin for town, so it names an urban resident, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Minter's conditions for ending the fight?

definitions.text: Minter's conditions for ending the fight?

parts.words: Minter's conditions for ending the fight?
parts.note: Alan Minter was a British boxer; the settlement under which a contest stops

explanation.surface: A boxer's demands before calling off a bout.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Minter was a British world middleweight boxing champion; his name also contains the letters, which may tempt a hidden-word search, but none runs through.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions agreed for settling a dispute are its stipulations.

clue.text: Duty-free

parts.note: not liable for a tax or obligation

explanation.definitionFit: Freed from a tax or obligation means not liable for it.

clue.text: A book brought out for the masses

definitions.text: A book brought out for the masses

parts.words: A book brought out for the masses
parts.note: masses here are Catholic church services, and the book is the one used at them

explanation.surface: A popular book published for ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the masses' suggests the general public, but means church Masses.
explanation.definitionFit: This liturgical book holds the texts for celebrating Mass through the year.

clue.text: Broken-heart from Afghan trade centre

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters of heart are reassembled

explanation.surface: Heartbreak coming out of an Afghan marketplace.
explanation.walkthrough: Herat is a city in western Afghanistan, long a trading hub on the Silk Road.
explanation.definitionFit: A major Afghan city and historic commercial hub on caravan routes.

clue.text: Organisation recruited to defend a Greek character?

explanation.surface: Volunteers enlisted to protect a Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force recruited for home defence; split as 'the TA', it gives the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Territorial Army reserve, written with its article; and the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: On coming in she was positively radiant

indicators.note: the word on comes into the middle of she

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman glowing as she arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' reads as a woman making an entrance, but it is the container signal; 'positively radiant' stretches the definition to a simple past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowed brightly, the past tense of a verb meaning to give out light.

clue.text: What the captain sounded when sailing past the Lorelei, for instance

definitions.text: What the captain sounded when sailing past the Lorelei, for instance

parts.words: What the captain sounded when sailing past the Lorelei, for instance
parts.note: a ship's warning horn, and also the singing temptress of the Rhine rock

explanation.surface: A ship's master passing the legendary Rhine rock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine where a singing maiden lured boatmen to their deaths: a warning hooter shares its name with such a temptress.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud warning hooter is sounded, and the Lorelei is a mythical female who lures sailors with song.

clue.text: No work is done when she takes the class

definitions.text: No work is done when she takes the class

parts.words: No work is done when she takes the class
parts.note: the teacher in charge of sport, whose lessons involve play rather than desk study

explanation.surface: A teacher whose lessons are slack.
explanation.walkthrough: The class plays sport rather than studying.
explanation.definitionFit: A school's PE teacher runs lessons of play and sport, not schoolwork.

clue.text: Political policy for sharing telephone costs

explanation.surface: A party's stance on splitting phone bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two senses: an official stance laid down by a party, and a phone line shared by several subscribers.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's official stance that members must follow; and a single telephone circuit shared by several households.
